What is the difference between `const` and `final` in Dart?
In programming, both "constant" (often denoted as `const`) and immutable variables are used to store values that do not change throughout their lifetime. However, there's a subtle but significant distinction when it comes to using them within classes or functions.

Constants (`const`) have compile-time evaluation guarantees; they must be initialized with an expression whose result can also be evaluated at compile time without any dependencies on runtime data like user input etc., hence making constants very efficient because these expressions get replaced during compilation itself rather than being computed every single run of your program which saves execution overheads significantly especially for large applications where performance matters greatly such as game engines written primarily in C++/C#/.NET languages often utilize this feature heavily since those environments allow similar constructs albeit slightly differently named e.g.: #define directive instead of const keyword usage directly inside code blocks unlike here we use top-level declarations only due historical reasons related back then how memory management worked compared nowdays more modern GC implementations available today). Constants declared outside methods/classes too follow same rules i.e.; cannot depend upon anything external other wise would violate its contract & cause errors while building project thus ensuring consistency across builds regardless OS/architecture targets chosen by developer.
